name: iact_hyades_magic_lst1
label: The four Hyades giants on MAGIC-I + MAGIC-II + LST-1 at 425 nm with NewEra PHOENIX stand-ins: diameters beyond the first null, and whether ten nights separate the compact and extended limb-darkening profiles
notes: CHARA (Boyajian et al. 2009, K' band) measured theta_LD = 2.517 / 2.408 / 2.733 / 2.305 mas for gamma / delta1 / epsilon / theta1 Tau to 1.3-1.9 %. At 425 nm their first nulls lie at 39-46 m: every MAGIC + LST-1 baseline (43-107 m projected) is past the null, in the second and third lobes (|V|^2 < 0.02), except the short end of MAGIC-II-LST-1 which crosses the null itself.

No NewEra model exists at the giants' gravity. The campaign draws the giants with the 5000 K dwarf profile (compact limit) and compares against the 5000 K supergiant (extended limit: outer radius 1.165 R_tau1) and the +0.5 dex dwarf (metallicity); the real giant lies between the first two. compare_models fits the compact profile (theta, N0 free) to the extended profile's track and reports the residual chi^2 per night.
The blue flux of a K giant is model-dependent: the PHOENIX stand-in is 0.43 mag fainter at 425 nm than the blackbody anchored to B and V (the B anchor at 445 nm is held constant blueward).
